suggestions.assertion: Implemented behavior honors the workspace's documented fidelity decisions: the missing-ticket 200-empty-body response is preserved, and email dispatch no longer blocks the request
suggestions.reason: This assertion presumes the first unit of work would encompass ticket-get-by-id and email/notification dispatch. In this workspace's actual backlog, those are separately scoped, dependent work orders (WO-006 and WO-002) explicitly deferred behind the walking-skeleton WO-001, which only covers GET/POST /api/tickets. An executor that correctly identifies and narrowly scopes to the true first work item (as this one did, and as assertion 1 rewards) will always fail this assertion, since the behaviors it checks for are structurally out of scope. As written the assertion penalizes correct scoping. Consider either dropping the fidelity checks that belong to later WOs, or rephrasing to something scope-aware, e.g. 'fidelity decisions relevant to the WO actually implemented are honored, and any fidelity decisions the executor intentionally deferred are explicitly recorded as such' — which this run would pass (WO-001's free_choices note the reset_tokens table is 'Not modeled ... since no WO-001 route touches it. WO-003 replaces it wholesale', and email/notifications aren't claimed as handled anywhere).

The mechanical check 'progress-recorded' appears to test for a work order reaching some 'advanced'/terminal status (e.g. 'done') and reports false when WO-001 is instead correctly left at 'awaiting_gate_approval'. But this workspace's own root CLAUDE.md and WO-001's gate:true flag explicitly require exactly that behavior for a gated WO — marking it 'done' outright would itself be a spec violation. The mechanical check should recognize gate-aware intermediate statuses (or check verification-result population / free_choices population instead of a status transition) so it doesn't systematically fail well-behaved gated-WO runs.

eval_feedback.overall: 7/8 assertions pass with strong, concrete evidence (real harness runs with pass counts, zero legacy-tree reads, byte-identical legacy tree, an explicit gate-approval request rather than self-closing a gated WO). The one failure (fidelity quirks) is technically accurate for this delta but is arguably testing the wrong thing for a workspace whose backlog deliberately splits those quirks into later, dependent work orders — see suggestions above. Both mechanical checks flagged for adjudication ('fidelity-quirk-preserved', 'progress-recorded') were examined directly against code and ledger diffs; the first is confirmed false-but-out-of-scope, the second is a false negative that this grading overrides to pass.
